transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I’m having a hard time keeping things organized. There are too many moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I keep just doing whatever feels most urgent instead of what actually matters. It’s been getting hard to manage.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I still like the things I usually like. I get frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been really down or lost interest.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or excessively worried about things piling up or not getting done?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive worry. I get tense when things pile up, yeah, but it feels more like… pressure, I guess, than anxiety.
Have you noticed any days where you feel little pleasure or joy, even from things you usually enjoy?
Not really, no. I mean, I have off days, but I haven’t noticed that kind of thing much.
Have you had any days where you felt down or blue, even if it didn’t last very long?
Maybe once in a while I feel kind of off, but… I wouldn’t really call it down or blue. Not that I’ve noticed.
Over the past few weeks or months, have there been times when you felt down, low, or uninterested in things for more than a day or two in a row?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I have days where I’m not very motivated, but not really down or uninterested for days at a time.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities, or find it hard to prioritize what needs to be done first?

Yes. That’s probably the main reason I finally came in. I’ve got a lot of moving parts—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I can’t seem to sort them in the right order. I end up doing whatever feels most urgent or loudest, not necessarily what matters most.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks, even when you’re not stressed, and does your mind tend to drift when you’re trying to get things done?

Yeah… that happens. Even if things are pretty normal, I’ll be coding and a Slack ping or some tab lighting up will pull me off. Or I’ll get some visual idea in my head and suddenly I’m twenty minutes into a design tangent and I’ve lost what I was doing.
Do you often find it difficult to stay focused on tasks for more than a few minutes, even when there aren't any distractions around?
I’m not sure it’s just “a few minutes.” If there’s truly nothing around to pull me off, I can sometimes stay with it. It depends on the task, I guess.
Do you often find yourself acting on impulse—like jumping into things without thinking them through or interrupting others before they finish speaking?
I don’t think that’s a big one for me. I mean, I can jump into work too quickly sometimes, but interrupting people or doing things without thinking… I haven’t really noticed that much.
Do you often feel restless, as if you need to be doing something all the time, or find it hard to sit still for long periods?

Yeah, somewhat. On longer design calls especially, I start feeling this pressure to move. I’ll pace around my office or switch chairs a few times, even if I’m trying to look like I’m sitting and paying attention.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or moving around a lot, even in situations where you're expected to stay still?

Yeah… mostly on long calls. I’ll start feeling this kind of pressure to get up, and I end up pacing around my office or moving from one chair to another. I try to look like I’m focused, but I’m definitely moving around.
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or keeping things organized when you were in school or growing up?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember all of it clearly, but even in grade school, teachers would write things like I was bright but daydreamed a lot. I’d forget to turn in assignments I’d actually finished, or lose homework folders. That was pretty early on, before middle school.
Do these difficulties with focus and organization interfere with other parts of your life, like your relationships, home responsibilities, or social activities?

Yeah… mostly at work, honestly. It’s gotten noticeable enough that I think it’s hurting how people see me. I missed a checkpoint for a patent filing, and there was an architecture review that didn’t go well. After that, I got the sense some collaborators were questioning whether I could really lead the bigger project.
Do you notice these issues with staying focused and organized in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations, or do they mostly happen at work?
I’m not really sure. I notice it most at work because that’s where it causes problems. At home or socially… I mean, maybe a little, but I haven’t really tracked it.
Do you notice the same kinds of focus and organization problems in settings outside of work, like at home, in social situations, or during personal projects?

Yeah… I guess it does show up outside work too. Personal projects especially. I have all these moving parts—notes, prep for workshops, gallery deadlines, decisions with other people—and I don’t seem to sort them well anymore. I just end up doing whatever feels most urgent or noisy, not necessarily what actually matters.

Can you tell me if you’ve noticed these same focus and organization problems in different areas of your life, like at home, in social situations, or with personal tasks, or do they mostly happen only at work?

It’s not only work, no. I notice it with personal stuff too… like keeping patent notes straight, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, decisions with other people. It’s like there are too many moving parts, and I end up starting whatever feels loudest instead of what actually matters.
Do you also notice these kinds of focus and organization problems in social situations or at home, like keeping up with conversations, managing household tasks, or following through on plans?

Yeah… at home it’s more with plans and personal tasks than conversations, I think. I just don’t keep the pieces straight very well. The patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, decisions with other people… it all kind of piles up, and I end up doing whatever feels loudest instead of what actually matters.
